dedupe_keys.name: university of bergen gnss data collection tec and scintillation at svalbard and bjørnøya 60 s since 2013

description: The University of Bergen Global Navigation Satellite System Data Collection, managed by the Birkeland Centre for Space Science and published on DataverseNO by Kjellmar Oksavik, holds total electron content and scintillation data at 60-second resolution from four NovAtel GPStation-6 ionospheric scintillation and TEC monitors installed in 2013 at Ny-Ålesund, Longyearbyen, Hopen and Bjørnøya in the Svalbard archipelago. Each receiver tracks GPS, GLONASS and Galileo signals on several frequencies. The data are organised in sub-datasets by year, station and parameter (TEC or scintillation), each with its own DOI, and a documentation dataset describes the file format and structure with MATLAB readers. Coverage: four high-Arctic stations from 2013, yearly files to 2024 at the time of reading. Format and access: yearly files on DataverseNO, free of charge under CC0. Caveats: four points under the polar cap and auroral oval; indices need expert interpretation; gaps where receivers failed. Simulation uses: long-term statistics of ionospheric disturbance and GNSS signal degradation at high latitude for hazard exposure and resilience studies of positioning and timing in Arctic shipping, aviation and communications. Related records: the May 2024 Arctic scintillation dataset covers one storm with more receivers; the CAS global TEC maps give global context; NOAA SWPC products give forecasts.
